subject.title: Onboarding Wizard should include Memory/Embedding setup as a mandatory step

question: Should first-run onboarding require a working embedding provider, prominently offer it with an explicit skip, or leave embedding setup to diagnostics and later configuration?
rationale: Current behavior supports keyword recall without embeddings, while mandatory remote credential collection, local-provider setup, SecretRef storage, and network probing each carry product and security tradeoffs that code inspection cannot decide.

options.title: Prominent optional setup
options.body: Add a first-class Memory step with provider, credential or SecretRef, and readiness guidance while allowing users to continue with clearly explained keyword-only recall.

options.title: Mandatory embedding gate
options.body: Require a successful remote or local embedding configuration before onboarding completes, accepting the added credential, network, and setup burden.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Keep onboarding unchanged and rely on doctor, memory status, and documentation to guide users after setup.

recommendation.title: Prominent optional setup
recommendation.body: Add a first-class Memory step with provider, credential or SecretRef, and readiness guidance while allowing users to continue with clearly explained keyword-only recall.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the assigned issue contact and already requested implementation follow-up, making them the best available owner for this product-policy choice.
